系.meaning: Grandma keeps one long <part>thread</part> that runs from her sewing box through every family photo on the wall, an ancestor knotted on at each one. Each new baby gets a little red <part>slash</part> of ink where it ties on. Follow it back and you see the whole <kanji>lineage</kanji>.
系.on: At every birthday a fresh knot is tied around the candles of the <sound>ca</sound>ke.

統.meaning: A weaver gathers <part>thread</part> from every village in the land and uses it to <part>fill</part> one enormous carpet, stitching all their patterns into a single design. Step back far enough and you see the whole kingdom at once: the <kanji>overall</kanji> picture.
統.on: Right in the middle she sews the king's big <sound>toe</sound>, poking out of his slipper.
統.kun: The king rules from the centre of the carpet, eating <sound>su</sound>shi off its pattern.

因.meaning: Something <part>large</part> is stuck in the <part>cage</part> in the kitchen, rattling the bars. Smashed plates, flour everywhere, the dog hiding: what started it all? The bars bend, and out climbs Grandpa, who went in after a cookie. He's the <kanji>cause</kanji>.
因.on: He leaves an <sound>in</sound>k footprint on every tile on his way out.
因.kun: It all began when his <sound>yo</sound>gurt pot rolled in there first.

敗.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> enters a sailing race with a paper <part>fan</part> as its only sail. It flaps and flaps, the boats zoom past, and then a seagull snatches the fan away. The shellfish sinks gently to the bottom: total <kanji>failure</kanji>.
敗.on: The seagull carries the fan off to a <sound>hi</sound>ve on the cliff, and the bees use it to cool their honey.
敗.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>! <sound>Boo</sound>!' jeer the crabs as the beaten shellfish crawls home.

掛.meaning: A tidy sailor has no cupboard, so he drives his <part>anchor</part> into a <part>double mound</part> of mud and uses its hooks as a rack. On go his hat, his boots, even a leaky <part>faucet</part> he found on the beach. He loves to <kanji>hang</kanji> things.
掛.on: Last of all he ties on the string of his <sound>ki</sound>te, which flutters above the mound all night.
掛.kun: Then a wet <sound>ca</sound>rp, hooked up by its tail to dry in the wind.

背.meaning: Two grumpy explorers at the <part>north</part> pole have had a row, so they sit back to back on a sledge under the <part>moon</part>, propping each other up. Neither will turn round all night. By dawn each knows every bump of the other's <kanji>back</kanji>.
背.on: A frozen <sound>hi</sound>ve sits wedged between their spines, humming and keeping them warm.
背.kun: A red <sound>se</sound>tter curls up and sleeps across their shoulders.

景.meaning: The <part>capital</part> charges ten coins to climb its tallest tower and watch the <part>sun</part> go down. At the top you find a single bench facing a brick wall, with a sunset painted on it. Still, everyone agrees it's lovely <kanji>scenery</kanji>.
景.on: Beside the bench, a man sells slices of <sound>ca</sound>ke shaped like little sunsets.
